candidates.title: Clinical Pathway Management for Platelet-Rich Plasma Therapy in Kellgren-Lawrence Grade I and II Knee Osteoarthritis: A Prospective, Multicenter, Double-Blind Randomized Controlled Trial.
candidates.authors_short: Yang S, Wang H, et al.
candidates.journal: The American journal of sports medicine
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND: Clinical outcomes after platelet-rich plasma (PRP) treatment for knee osteoarthritis are inconsistent, and some well-designed trials show no benefit. Whether a standardized multicomponent pathway improves outcomes relative to conventional PRP care is uncertain. PURPOSE: To compare the efficacy, safety, satisfaction, and costs of a standardized PRP pathway versus physician-directed conventional PRP care in Kellgren-Lawrence grade I and II knee osteoarthritis. STUDY DESIGN: Randomized controlled trial; Level of evidence, 1. METHODS: At 3 hospitals, 240 patients were randomized 1:1 to a standardized PRP clinical pathway (PRP-CP; n = 120) or physician-directed conventional PRP care (PRP-C; n = 120). PRP-CP combined standardized selection, quality-controlled leukocyte-poor PRP, ultrasound-guided injections, staged rehabilitation, and systematic follow-up. Primary 12-month outcomes were visual analog scale (VAS) pain, Western Ontario and McMaster Universities Osteoarthritis Index (WOMAC) total, and International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC) scores; secondary outcomes included achievement of the minimal clinically important difference, satisfaction, adverse events, and costs. RESULTS: At 12 months, PRP-CP produced greater changes than PRP-C in VAS (mean difference [MD], -2.98 [95% CI, -3.64 to -2.32]), WOMAC total (MD, -8.63 [95% CI, -11.35 to -5.90]), and IKDC (MD, 10.25 [95% CI, 8.37 to 12.13]) scores (all P < .001). Achievement of the minimal clinically important difference favored PRP-CP at 3, 6, and 12 months for the VAS and at 6 and 12 months for the IKDC and WOMAC (P < .05). Satisfaction was greater with PRP-CP (odds ratio, 1.79 [95% CI, 1.11-2.89]; P = .017). An adverse event occurred in 17 of 115 patients in the PRP-CP group (14.8%) versus 36 of 113 patients in the PRP-C group (31.9%) (Fisher exact test: P = .003). Mean costs were CN¥15,199.9 versus CN¥14,754.4, respectively; the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio was CN¥66.0 per WOMAC point. Effects were generally consistent across centers, and blinding was maintained. CONCLUSION: The standardized multicomponent pathway produced greater 12-month improvements in pain and function than conventional PRP care, with fewer adverse events. Because components were bundled and no placebo group was included, the trial does not establish PRP efficacy or component-specific effects.
candidates.score_reasoning: High-quality RCT from AJSM evaluating a standardized PRP pathway versus conventional PRP care for early knee OA with 240 patients and clinically meaningful outcome differences, directly applicable to practice given widespread PRP use.
bullets: In adults with early knee osteoarthritis (KL grade I/II), a standardized PRP pathway combining quality-controlled injection, ultrasound guidance, and staged rehab produced meaningfully greater pain and function gains at 12 months than standard physician-directed PRP care.
The structured pathway also cut adverse events roughly in half (15% vs 32%) with only a marginal cost increase, making it a safer option for this patient group.
Clinically, this suggests that how PRP is delivered matters as much as the injection itself, though the trial does not prove PRP works better than placebo.

candidates.title: Short-term benefits of hybrid graft in medial patellofemoral ligament reconstruction for recurrent patellar dislocation: A prospective randomized controlled trial with minimum 2-year follow-up.
candidates.authors_short: Zhang X, Zhai W, et al.
candidates.journal: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA
candidates.abstract: PURPOSE: This study aimed to compare short-term functional and radiological outcomes between autograft and hybrid graft reconstruction in medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) reconstruction for recurrent patellar dislocation and explore reasons for differences. METHODS: This prospective randomized controlled trial enroled 51 patients with recurrent patellar dislocation undergoing MPFL reconstruction between January 2020 and January 2023. Major exclusions included severe trochlear dysplasia (Dejour Type B-D), open physis, patella alta, severe lower limb malalignment (knee valgus angle >20°, femoral anteversion >25° or external tibial torsion >30°) and tibial tubercle-trochlear groove (TT-TG) distance ≥20 mm. Patients were randomly assigned to autograft or hybrid graft groups; the hybrid graft comprised a semitendinosus tendon and 6-mm artificial ligament tape. The primary outcome was the 12-month Kujala score, prespecified for early functional recovery. Secondary outcomes included Kujala and International Knee Documentation Committee (IKDC) scores at other time points and imaging parameters (patellar lateral tilt [PLT] angle and patellar-trochlear groove [PTG] distance) preoperatively, immediately postoperatively and at final follow-up. RESULTS: Forty-six patients were included in the final analysis (autograft, n = 22; hybrid graft, n = 24). Mean age was 19.3 years; 82.6% (38/46) were female. Baseline characteristics and preoperative functional scores were comparable between groups (all p > 0.05). Significant improvements in subjective knee scores were observed in both groups at 3, 6, 12 months and final follow-up (p < 0.05). At 3 months, mean Kujala and IKDC scores were 68.6 ± 5.2 and 68.0 ± 6.1 in the autograft group versus 82.4 ± 4.3 and 82.9 ± 3.3 in the hybrid graft group (both p < 0.001). At 6 months, corresponding scores were 83.4 ± 3.6 and 83.3 ± 3.3 versus 88.4 ± 4.6 and 88.0 ± 4.9 (both p < 0.05). No significant between-group differences were observed at 12 months or final follow-up (all p > 0.05). No significant between-group differences in PLT angle and PTG distance were observed immediately postoperatively or at final follow-up (all p > 0.05), with significant improvements from preoperative values in both groups (p < 0.05). CONCLUSION: In carefully selected patients with recurrent patellar dislocation, MPFL reconstruction using a hybrid graft achieved satisfactory short-term clinical and radiographic outcomes and was associated with improved early functional recovery at 3 and 6 months. The hybrid graft may be a feasible option for MPFL reconstruction. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level II.
candidates.score_reasoning: Prospective RCT from JBJS comparing MPFL autograft versus hybrid graft reconstruction with 2-year minimum follow-up, directly applicable to a common surgical decision point with clear functional and radiological outcomes.
bullets: In young patients with recurrent patellar dislocation and no major bony deformity, hybrid graft MPFL reconstruction produced better knee function scores at 3 and 6 months compared to autograft alone.
By 12 months and at final follow-up, functional scores and patellar alignment were equivalent between hybrid graft and autograft groups, with no redislocations reported in either group.
For surgeons performing MPFL reconstruction, adding an artificial ligament tape to the semitendinosus graft may accelerate early recovery without sacrificing medium-term outcomes.

candidates.title: Long-term survivorship of medial meniscus posterior horn repair during revision anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: 10-year results from the SANTI Group.
candidates.authors_short: Santamaria F, Wehbe H, et al.
candidates.journal: Knee surgery, sports traumatology, arthroscopy : official journal of the ESSKA
candidates.abstract: PURPOSE: To evaluate the long-term rate of secondary medial meniscectomy following medial meniscus posterior horn repair performed during revision anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (ACLR) and to compare contemporary posteromedial suture-hook repair with other repair strategies used during the study period. We hypothesized that suture-hook repair would be associated with improved long-term meniscal survivorship compared to other repair strategies performed with revision ACLR. METHODS: This retrospective cohort study included patients undergoing revision anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction (rACLR) between 2003 and 2023 at a single high-volume centre. Knees presenting with ramp lesions, meniscocapsular separations, meniscotibial disruptions and longitudinal vertical tears extending into the posterior horn of the medial meniscus treated by repair were identified and stratified according to repair strategy: contemporary posteromedial suture-hook repair versus other techniques used during the study period, including all-inside, inside-out and earlier repair techniques. The primary outcome was secondary medial meniscectomy. Time-to-event analysis was performed using Kaplan-Meier survival estimates and compared using the log-rank test. A multivariable Cox proportional hazards model was used to assess independent predictors of secondary medial meniscectomy, with administrative censoring at 10 years. RESULTS: A total of 402 medial meniscus repairs were included, with a mean follow-up of 96.0 ± 31.4 months after administrative censoring at 10 years. At 10 years, the cumulative rate of secondary medial meniscectomy was 17.5% (95% confidence interval [CI] 13.6-22.4). Unadjusted analysis demonstrated a lower rate of secondary medial meniscectomy in the suture-hook repair group compared with other repair techniques used during the study period (15.8% [95% CI 11.3-21.9] vs. 24.1% [95% CI 16.3-34.9]; log-rank p = 0.0499). However, after multivariable adjustment, repair technique was not independently associated with secondary medial meniscectomy (hazard ratio 1.62, 95% CI 0.90-2.83; p = 0.0986). CONCLUSION: Long-term outcomes of medial meniscus posterior horn repair during rACLR showed a 17.5% cumulative rate of secondary medial meniscectomy at 10 years. Posteromedial suture-hook repair was associated with lower failure rates than other repair techniques on unadjusted analysis; however, repair technique was not an independent predictor of secondary medial meniscectomy after multivariable adjustment. These findings support meniscal preservation and systematic assessment of posteromedial meniscal lesions during revision ACLR while providing realistic long-term expectations regarding repair survivorship. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, retrospective cohort study.
candidates.score_reasoning: Large prospective registry-based cohort study identifying sex-specific risk factors for stiffness after ACLR including graft type and meniscus repair, with immediate surgical decision-making implications.
bullets: In 402 medial meniscus posterior horn repairs performed during revision ACL reconstruction, roughly 1 in 6 patients required secondary meniscectomy within 10 years.
This failure rate applies to revision ACL patients with ramp lesions, meniscocapsular separations, and posterior horn tears who underwent meniscal repair regardless of suture technique used.

Surgeons should repair medial meniscus posterior horn lesions during revision ACL reconstruction but should counsel patients that about 17 percent will ultimately need meniscectomy over the following decade.

candidates.title: Comparison of Shoulder Field Anesthesia (SFA) with Interscalene Block (ISB) for Analgesia After Arthroscopic Shoulder Surgery: A Randomized Noninferiority Trial.
candidates.authors_short: Qawasmi F, Gazit T, et al.
candidates.journal: The Journal of bone and joint surgery. American volume
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND: An interscalene brachial plexus block (ISB) is commonly used for analgesia after shoulder surgery but is associated with neurologic and respiratory complications, including hemidiaphragmatic paralysis. Surgeon-performed shoulder field anesthesia (SFA) is a landmark-guided, phrenic nerve-sparing technique that may provide effective analgesia with fewer complications. The purpose of this study was to compare SFA with ISB for pain control after arthroscopic shoulder surgery. We investigated whether SFA would provide noninferior analgesia as measured by cumulative 48-hour postoperative pain scores. METHODS: In this randomized trial, patients undergoing arthroscopic shoulder surgery were assigned to SFA or ISB. Postoperative pain was assessed using the numeric rating scale (NRS) at 2, 4, 8, 24, and 48 hours. Patient satisfaction was assessed at 48 hours. Other secondary outcomes included opioid consumption, hospital stay, and block-related complications. RESULTS: Eighty patients (mean age, 47.7 ± 15.7 years; 53 men) completed the study. All patients were classified as White; 80% were of Middle Eastern ethnicity. Baseline characteristics were comparable between the SFA and ISB groups. The primary outcome analysis demonstrated a mean difference in the cumulative 48-hour NRS pain score of -0.824 (ISB - SFA), with a 95% confidence interval of -1.853 to 0.206. The upper limit of the confidence interval remained below the prespecified noninferiority margin of 1.5 NRS points, demonstrating noninferiority of SFA. ISB provided lower pain scores during the early postoperative period (4 to 8 hours), and pain scores converged thereafter. Hospital stay was shorter in the SFA group. Opioid consumption, patient satisfaction, and oxygen desaturation rates were similar between groups. Two cases of Horner syndrome and 1 respiratory event requiring intensive care occurred in the ISB group; none occurred in the SFA group. CONCLUSIONS: SFA was noninferior to ISB for the prespecified cumulative 48-hour pain end point. ISB provided superior pain relief during the first 4 to 8 hours, but SFA offered a lung-sparing alternative with similar cumulative opioid requirements and patient satisfaction, fewer clinically apparent block-related complications, and a shorter hospital stay. These findings support a risk-benefit framework to guide individualized analgesic selection. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Therapeutic Level I. See Instructions for Authors for a complete description of levels of evidence.
candidates.score_reasoning: RCT from JBJS comparing shoulder field anesthesia to interscalene block for arthroscopic shoulder surgery, demonstrating noninferiority with fewer complications, directly impacting perioperative anesthesia planning.
bullets: Surgeon-performed shoulder field anesthesia matched interscalene block for total pain control over 48 hours after arthroscopic shoulder surgery, with similar opioid use and patient satisfaction.
Interscalene block provided better pain relief in the first 4 to 8 hours, but complications including Horner syndrome and one ICU-level respiratory event occurred only in the interscalene group.
For patients where phrenic nerve palsy or respiratory compromise is a concern, shoulder field anesthesia is a viable alternative that spares the lung and shortens hospital stay.

candidates.title: Polyethylene glenospheres in reverse total shoulder arthroplasty have greater long-term implant survivorship than metallic glenospheres: A New Zealand Joint Registry Study.
candidates.authors_short: Bayley S, Boyle AB, et al.
candidates.journal: Journal of shoulder and elbow surgery
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND: Reverse total shoulder arthroplasty (rTSA) is increasingly common and clinically effective. Conventional-bearing rTSA (CB-rTSA) employs a metallic glenosphere articulating with a polyethylene humeral liner. Inverted-bearing rTSA (IB-rTSA), using a polyethylene glenosphere with a metallic or ceramic humeral liner, was developed to eliminate polyethylene wear debris at the scapular neck and thereby reduce polyethylene-induced osteolysis and the severity of scapular notching. Comparative data on survivorship and patient-reported outcomes between these configurations remain limited. This study compared implant survival, revision risk and functional outcomes between CB-rTSA and IB-rTSA designs. METHODS: This retrospective comparative cohort study identified all primary rTSA procedures performed in New Zealand between January 2007 and December 2024 from the New Zealand Joint Registry. Revision-free implant survival and postoperative function, measured by the Oxford Shoulder Score (OSS), were analysed. Patients were grouped by bearing configuration: polyethylene glenosphere (IB-rTSA) and metal glenosphere (CB-rTSA). Subgroup analyses compared SMR Reverse Polyethylene and SMR Reverse Metal (LimaCorporate, Italy) with other CB-rTSA designs, predominantly Delta Xtend (DePuy Synthes, USA). Revision rates per 100 component-years were calculated, and multivariable Cox proportional hazards models compared revision risk, adjusting for age, sex and diagnosis. RESULTS: A total of 8,601 rTSA procedures were included: 3,437 (40.0%) using a polyethylene glenosphere and 5,164 (60.0%) a metallic glenosphere. Indications for surgery were comparable between groups, whereas the sex distribution differed significantly. Unadjusted revision rates per 100 component-years were higher for the metal group (0.71) than the polyethylene group (0.46) (P = .001). The adjusted hazard ratio for polyethylene compared with metal was 0.57 (95% CI 0.43 - 0.75), representing a 43% lower revision rate. In secondary, unadjusted cause-specific analyses, polyethylene glenospheres were associated with fewer revisions for deep infection (0.11 vs 0.20 per 100 component-years; P = .031) and dislocation (0.09 vs 0.16; P = .045). Mean OSS at 6 months, 5 years and 10 years were similar between groups, with no statistically or clinically significant differences. CONCLUSION: In this large national registry study, IB-rTSA using a polyethylene glenosphere was associated with significantly lower revision rates than conventional metal glenosphere designs, with no statistically or clinically significant differences in patient-reported functional outcomes. In secondary, unadjusted cause-specific analyses, polyethylene glenospheres were also associated with lower rates of revision for deep infection and dislocation. Although it could not be examined using registry data, this lower revision burden may relate to the absence of polyethylene-induced osteolysis and consequently less pronounced scapular notching.
candidates.score_reasoning: Multicenter prospective RCT with 240 patients evaluating a structured PRP clinical pathway versus conventional PRP for knee OA, showing clinically significant improvements across all PRO measures at 12 months.
bullets: In over 8,600 reverse shoulder replacements from the New Zealand Joint Registry, polyethylene glenospheres had a 43% lower revision rate than metal glenospheres over long-term follow-up.
Polyethylene glenosphere designs were also associated with lower revision rates for deep infection and dislocation, with no difference in shoulder function scores at any time point.

For surgeons choosing a reverse shoulder implant, a polyethylene glenosphere bearing surface appears to offer a survivorship advantage over conventional metal glenosphere designs without sacrificing patient outcomes.

candidates.title: Association of Changes in Game Pitch Count, Pitching Velocity, and Arm Injuries in Collegiate Pitchers.
candidates.authors_short: Salamh P, Plisky P, et al.
candidates.journal: The American journal of sports medicine
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND: Baseball pitchers experience a high rate of shoulder and elbow injuries. While there have been several factors associated with arm injuries among pitchers, pitch volume and pitch velocity have garnered a great deal of attention. The associations among pitch counts, pitch velocity, and arm injury have not been well studied. PURPOSE: To assess the association between changes in game pitch count and arm injuries in collegiate baseball pitchers over 1 summer season. The secondary aim was to assess the association between mean in-game fastball pitch velocity and arm injuries in the same baseball pitchers. STUDY DESIGN: Cohort study; Level of evidence, 2. METHODS: Collegiate pitchers were prospectively followed throughout the summer season for game pitch count, pitch velocity, and arm injuries. Bayesian joint models, including time-to-event Cox regressions and multilevel mixed effects regressions, were performed to assess the associations of interest, while competing risks of release and/or retirement were controlled for. Nonlinear relationships were modeled using natural splines. Change in pitch count and pitch velocity was modeled by the change in each pitcher's mean seasonal pitch count or pitch velocity. RESULTS: A total of 187 pitchers were included in this study and followed for a total of 9890 baseball exposure days. A total of 22 pitchers (12%; 95% CI, 7.5%-17.2%) experienced an arm injury, and 4 pitchers (2%; 95% CI, 0.6%-5.4%) were released, voluntarily retired, or reached their innings limit for the season. There was a nonlinear (parabolic shape) positive association of an increased change in pitch count as compared with the pitcher's mean pitch count and arm injuries. Additionally, there was a nonlinear (parabolic shape) positive association between arm injury hazard and a decrease in fastball pitch velocity when compared with the pitcher's mean fastball pitch velocity. CONCLUSION: There was an increased risk for shoulder and elbow injuries with an increase in pitch count as compared with a pitcher's mean pitch count over pitch appearances. Additionally, there was an association between arm injuries and decreased pitch velocity as compared with a pitcher's mean pitch velocity.
candidates.score_reasoning: Multicenter case-control study from CORR addressing whether prior failed DAIR increases reinfection risk after two-stage revision PJI—a clinically critical and frequently encountered decision point with meaningful sample size.
bullets: Collegiate pitchers who threw more pitches than their personal seasonal average had a higher risk of shoulder and elbow injury, with risk rising in a nonlinear pattern as pitch count deviated upward.
A drop in fastball velocity below a pitcher's personal average was also associated with increased arm injury risk, suggesting velocity loss is a clinically useful early warning sign.

Monitoring individual pitch count spikes and velocity declines, rather than relying on fixed thresholds, may help team orthopaedic staff identify collegiate pitchers at elevated injury risk before symptoms develop.

candidates.title: Osteoporosis Screening Gaps Among Patients Undergoing Lumbar Fusion Surgery.
candidates.authors_short: Mao E, Ceballos-Alvarez KE, et al.
candidates.journal: The Journal of the American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND: Osteoporosis is associated with elevated complication rates after lumbar fusion surgery. Despite this, osteoporosis remains both underscreened and undertreated in the United States. Currently, rates of dual-energy radiograph absorptiometry (DEXA) screening before lumbar fusion surgery are unknown, as is the proportion of patients who, after being diagnosed with osteoporosis, receive appropriate treatment. Therefore, the aim of this study was to assess osteoporosis screening and treatment rates among patients undergoing lumbar fusion surgery. METHODS: Patients older than 50 years undergoing lumbar fusion for lumbar stenosis with degenerative spondylolisthesis were identified using the TriNetX database. Patients receiving surgery for indications of malignancy or infection, as well as those with diagnoses of osteoporosis before the screening window, were excluded. The prevalence of DEXA scans in the 2 years before fusion was calculated for the overall cohort and for high-risk cohorts defined by Endocrinology Society guidelines. A secondary analysis assessed rates of osteoporosis treatment among patients receiving preoperative DEXA scans. RESULTS: Of 46,104 patients who underwent lumbar fusion surgery, only 4.5% of men and 15.6% of women received a preoperative DEXA scan in the 2 years before their fusion. Women were more likely to receive DEXA scans than men (OR, 3.93; 95% CI, 3.64 to 4.23; P < 0.001). Only 5.6% of high-risk men and 17.5% of high-risk women received preoperative DEXA screening. Among patients diagnosed with osteoporosis after DEXA screening, only 11.0% received anabolic therapy and 23.1% received antiresorptive therapy. CONCLUSION: Despite most patients undergoing lumbar fusion being at risk of osteoporosis (and eligible for screening), a small minority were screened using DEXA in the 2 years before surgery. Efforts are warranted to increase the prevalence of DEXA screening so that osteoporosis is appropriately diagnosed and treated before lumbar fusion surgery.
candidates.score_reasoning: Large NSQIP-based retrospective study developing and validating a preoperative bedside tool (SHORD Score) to predict non-home discharge after TSA, with strong discrimination and direct preoperative counseling utility.
bullets: Among over 46,000 patients undergoing lumbar fusion, only 4.5% of men and 15.6% of women received a DEXA scan in the two years before surgery.
Even among high-risk patients flagged by Endocrinology Society criteria, preoperative DEXA screening rates remained similarly low for both men and women.
Of those diagnosed with osteoporosis before fusion, fewer than one in four received any medical treatment, leaving most at elevated risk for hardware failure and complications.

candidates.title: Sepsis Prior to Total Knee Arthroplasty is Associated With Elevated Rates of Myocardial Infarction and Deep Vein Thrombosis.
candidates.authors_short: Alhankawi AR, Holle AM, et al.
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND: Patients who have sepsis often experience persistent physiological instability, which may increase vulnerability to postoperative complications. However, the impact of preoperative sepsis on outcomes following elective total knee arthroplasty (TKA) remains poorly defined. Thus, the purpose of this study was to investigate the association of preoperative sepsis with 90-day and two-year postoperative complications following TKA. METHODS: A retrospective study was conducted utilizing an insurance database. Patients who had a preoperative diagnosis of sepsis within two years prior to TKA were matched 1:3 to controls based on demographics and comorbidities. Patients who had sepsis were stratified according to the following timeline: sepsis three months prior to surgery, three to six months prior, six to 12 months prior, 12 to 18 months prior, and 18 to 24 months prior. Medical and surgical complications were assessed at 90 days and two years following surgery. Statistical significance was set at P < 0.05. RESULTS: Patients who had sepsis within two years prior to surgery exhibited increased rates of periprosthetic joint infection (PJI) (odds ratio (OR): 1.6), postoperative sepsis (OR: 2.7), acute kidney injury (OR: 1.4), urinary tract infection (OR: 1.8), blood transfusion (OR: 2.0), readmission (OR: 1.3), and wound dehiscence (OR: 1.4) within 90 days of surgery. At two years following surgery, sepsis was associated with elevated rates of revision surgery (OR: 1.3), PJI (OR: 1.6), osteomyelitis (OR: 1.9), and mortality (OR: 1.3). Sepsis within three months of operation was associated with elevated rates of myocardial infarction (OR: 2.1) and deep vein thrombosis (OR: 2.0). All findings were statistically significant at P < 0.05. CONCLUSION: Preoperative sepsis is associated with increased complications following TKA, including periprosthetic joint infection and mortality. Sepsis within three months of surgery confers a particularly elevated risk of myocardial infarction and deep vein thrombosis following TKA.
candidates.score_reasoning: Large retrospective database study (77,958 patients) from Journal of Arthroplasty examining SSRI use and dose-response on THA complications, providing actionable preoperative risk stratification data.
bullets: Patients with sepsis in the two years before TKA face higher rates of periprosthetic joint infection, readmission, revision surgery, and death compared to matched controls.
Sepsis within three months of TKA roughly doubles the risk of myocardial infarction and deep vein thrombosis in the postoperative period.
Orthopaedic surgeons should carefully weigh timing of elective TKA in patients with recent sepsis, particularly within the preceding three months.

candidates.title: Total Hip Arthroplasty Is Associated With Lower 90-Day Inpatient Readmission Than Hemiarthroplasty for Femoral Neck Fracture in Patients Aged 65-75 Years: A Propensity Score-Matched Nationwide Readmissions Database Study.
candidates.authors_short: Maman D, Steinfeld Y, Berkovich Y
candidates.abstract: BACKGROUND: Comparative early hospital-based outcomes of hemiarthroplasty and total hip arthroplasty (THA) for femoral neck fracture remain uncertain in patients aged 65-75 years. METHODS: Using the 2022 Nationwide Readmissions Database, we identified patients aged 65-75 years admitted with an acute femoral neck fracture who underwent hemiarthroplasty or THA. Patients were matched 1:1 using exact matching on age, Hospital Frailty Risk Score category, and mental-disorder status, plus propensity-score matching with a 0.20-standard-deviation caliper. The primary outcome was all-cause inpatient readmission within 90 days. RESULTS: Among 8,012 eligible admissions, 5,108 patients underwent hemiarthroplasty and 2,904 underwent THA. Matching yielded 2,702 patients per group, with all postmatch absolute standardized mean differences <0.10. THA was associated with a lower observed 90-day inpatient readmission rate than hemiarthroplasty (10.1% vs 15.7%; odds ratio, 0.60; 95% confidence interval, 0.51-0.71; P < .001). Death during the first readmission was also less frequent after THA (0.1% vs 0.7%; P = .002). A narrowly defined inpatient principal-diagnosis dislocation indicator did not differ significantly between groups and should not be interpreted as overall dislocation incidence. Index and total 90-day hospital charges were higher with THA. CONCLUSIONS: In this observational claims-based study, THA was associated with a lower observed 90-day inpatient readmission rate than hemiarthroplasty. Residual selection bias may partly explain this association, and these findings do not establish a causal benefit of THA. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level III, Retrospective comparative study.
candidates.score_reasoning: Propensity-matched nationwide readmissions database study comparing THA versus hemiarthroplasty in patients aged 65–75 with femoral neck fracture, showing lower 90-day readmission with THA—directly relevant to a common clinical decision.
bullets: In patients aged 65 to 75 years with femoral neck fracture, THA was associated with a 90-day readmission rate of 10.1% compared to 15.7% for hemiarthroplasty in a propensity-matched national cohort.
Death at first readmission was rare but less frequent after THA than hemiarthroplasty (0.1% vs 0.7%), though index hospital charges were higher with THA.

For otherwise healthy patients aged 65 to 75 with femoral neck fracture, this data supports reconsidering hemiarthroplasty as the default implant choice, though selection bias in this observational study cannot be excluded.

candidates.title: Delphi Consensus on Periprosthetic Surgical Irrigation: Safety and Tissue Compatibility.
candidates.score_reasoning: Large retrospective database study showing preoperative sepsis is significantly associated with elevated PJI, MI, DVT, and revision rates after TKA, providing important preoperative risk stratification guidance.
bullets: A Delphi consensus panel reached agreement on recommended irrigation solutions considered safe for periprosthetic tissues during revision arthroplasty.
The guidance applies to orthopaedic surgeons managing periprosthetic joint infections or performing revision procedures where irrigation choice affects tissue viability.
Surgeons should follow consensus-backed irrigation protocols to reduce tissue toxicity risk while maintaining adequate wound decontamination.
